62_marg1586: Or the three heavens are understood as three kinds of visions, so that the first heaven is bodily vision, when certain things are seen bodily by the gift of God, as Eliseus saw the fiery chariots when Elias was taken up; and Baltasar the hand writing on the wall: “Mane, Thecel, Phares.” The second heaven is imaginary or spiritual vision, when someone in ecstasy or in sleep sees not bodies but images of things by the revelation of God, as Peter the sheet. The third heaven is intellectual vision, when neither bodies nor their images are seen, but the gaze of the mind is fixed, by the wondrous power of God, on incorporeal substances. To this the Apostle was caught up, that he might see God himself in himself, not in any figure. But whether in the body or in the separated soul, he says he does not know. As if to say: I did not see by human sense, so that, even if in the body, it is not against that word of Moses: “Man shall not see me and live.” For then the Apostle did not live as a man, that is, according to the use of the senses of the body, but every sense of man was taken away. Or, according to Dionysius, who established three orders of angels, placing three in each: in the first, angels, archangels, virtues; in the second, principalities, powers, dominations; in the third, thrones, cherubim and seraphim, the third of which contemplates God more nearly; in likeness to these the Apostle is said to have seen God. Or the first heaven is the knowledge of the heavenly bodies, the second the knowledge of the heavenly spirits, the third the knowledge of the Godhead.
62_marg1587: The third heaven, which is not seen through the body, nor imaginatively but properly, is seen by that vision which surpasses all. Through the body are seen heaven, earth, and all things visible to the eyes. The spirit holds bodily images, either true ones or such as it feigns. The intellect grasps incorporeal things, which have no images. These are the three kinds of visions. By the first vision Baltasar saw the hand, and did not know what it signified, which Daniel, a prophet, better by the proper vision of the mind, explained. By the second Peter saw the sheet in ecstasy, where not the body but the image, and afterwards the mind divinely aided, saw what it signified. Borne up to this, the mind without any image sees the clear truth; there the powers of the soul are without any labour; there the whole power is one: to love what you see, and the highest happiness is to see and to have what you love. For the sake of this vision of the truth, where God is seen, not by bodily vision as on Sina, or spiritual, as Isaias and John in the Apocalypse, but “by sight, not in a riddle,” every labour is undertaken. In this way Moses asked to see God, that is, in the substance which is God, whom yet he had seen in many figures, and to whom he had spoken face to face. Because there, that is, in that species, he is seen far more ineffably and more powerfully, and speaks hidden things, where no one living in these senses sees. This is the third heaven, where God is seen face to face. This is paradise, if it can be called paradise, because both the present Church is called paradise and the place in which Adam lived bodily.
